title: An envoy brings betel
story: An envoy from {neighbor} arrives at the Bahay ng Datu with a gift of betel nut and lime, sent by {datu} as a greeting between datus. How will you receive them?

choices.label: Receive them with a meal
choices.result: You chew betel together and share a meal. The envoy carries warm words home to {datu}.

choices.label: Accept the gift politely
choices.result: You accept the betel and send the envoy home with your greetings.

choices.label: Refuse the gift
choices.result: The envoy leaves with the betel still in hand. {datu} will hear of the insult.

_note: Offering and chewing betel (nganga) together was a common courtesy and part of meetings, agreements and rites.
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994), on betel chewing in social life
